source_quote: 6 credit restricted Departmental Electives
answer: Civil engineering technical electives (level 400 or above) consist of 6 credits of restricted departmental electives and 9 credits from any engineering discipline at the 400 level or above.

source_quote: Code numbers designate the courses offered in the Civil Engineering program in the
answer: CIVE course codes 'CIVE abc': a = year (2 first, 3 second, 4 third, 5 fourth year); b = area (0 Common/Construction Management, 1 Structural Analysis and Design, 2 Construction Materials and Geotechnics, 4 Public Works, 7 Water Resources and Treatment); c = sequence 0-9.

source_quote: Brief review of statics; proper use of different coordinate systems: Cartesian and
answer: MECH 220 Dynamics, 3(3,0): kinematics and kinetics of particles and planar rigid bodies (force and acceleration, work and energy, impulse and momentum) with coordinate systems; offered annually.

source_quote: momentum. Prerequisite: CIVE 211. Annually.
answer: The prerequisite for MECH 220 Dynamics is CIVE 211 Statics.

source_quote: Mechanical stress, strain, and stress/strain relations under pure tension, compression,
answer: MECH 320 Mechanics of Materials, 3(3,0): stress, strain, tension, compression, bending and torsion, thermal stress, combined and principal stresses, Mohr's circle, 3-D elasticity and column buckling. Prerequisite: CIVE 211.

source_quote: This course seeks to impart fundamental concepts of thermal-fluid (including
answer: MECH 333 Thermal Fluid Sciences, 3(3,0): thermodynamics, fluid mechanics and heat transfer for non-mechanical engineering students - properties, first law, fluid statics, Bernoulli, conservation laws, pipe flow and conduction/convection/radiation. Prerequisite: MATH 216.

source_quote: A broad introductory course that exposes students to the history and heritage of civil
answer: CIVE 200 Introduction to Civil Engineering, 2(2,0): history of civil engineering, its sub-disciplines, professional challenges, registration and societies, codes and standards, and business aspects such as construction management and engineering economics.

source_quote: Essential engineering drawing concepts for civil and architectural applications, along
answer: CIVE 202 Civil and Architectural Drawings, 3(2,2): engineering drawing and 2D/3D computer drafting for floor plans, sections, elevations and reinforcement detailing, with symbols and annotation for site construction. Prerequisite: None.

source_quote: Static laws; force vectors and operations; force systems and moments; free-body
answer: CIVE 211 Statics, 3(3,0): force vectors and systems, moments, free-body diagrams, equilibrium in 2D/3D, trusses, frames, cables, shear and moment diagrams, centroids, moment of inertia and friction. Prerequisite: None.

source_quote: Surveying fundamentals; theory of errors in observations; leveling; distance
answer: CIVE 240 Surveying, 3(2,2): errors in observations, leveling, distance and angle measurement, traversing, topographic surveys and maps, with group field surveys and technical reports. Prerequisite: None.

source_quote: Shear and bending moment diagrams for frames, equilibrium, stability, and
answer: CIVE 312 Structural Analysis I, 3(3,0): shear and moment diagrams for frames, stability and determinacy, influence lines, elastic deformation of beams, frames and trusses, and introduction to indeterminate structures.

source_quote: frames, and trusses; introduction to indeterminate structures. Prerequisite: MECH
answer: The prerequisite for CIVE 312 Structural Analysis I is MECH 320.

source_quote: Behavior of reinforced concrete structural elements; concepts of design and
answer: CIVE 314 Concrete I, 3(3,0): reinforced concrete behavior, flexure and shear design of beams, crack width and deflection, one-way solid and joist slabs, bond, development, anchorage and splicing of reinforcement.

source_quote: continuous beams and one-way slabs. Prerequisite: MECH 320. Annually.
answer: The prerequisite for CIVE 314 Concrete I is MECH 320.

source_quote: Properties and tests of materials used in the construction of civil structures, such as
answer: CIVE 321 Construction Materials, 3(3,0): properties and testing of aggregate, cement, admixtures, steel, masonry, concrete, asphalt and timber, with emphasis on fresh and hardened concrete and mix design.

source_quote: Los Angeles abrasion test; specific gravity and absorption of coarse and fine
answer: CIVE 321L Construction Materials Laboratory, 1(0,2): aggregate and soil tests, sieve analysis, concrete mix design, slump and compressive strength tests, masonry unit tests and report writing. Co-requisite: CIVE 321.

source_quote: Introduction to highway engineering standards; types and classifications of roads;
answer: CIVE 341 Highway Engineering, 3(3,0): road classification, driver/vehicle/road characteristics, highway location, earthwork, geometric design (alignment, curves, superelevation, intersections), materials, construction, quality control and maintenance. Prerequisite: CIVE 240.

source_quote: Social and economic impact of traffic engineering on society; basis of traffic
answer: CIVE 342 Traffic Engineering, 3(3,0): transportation planning, traffic flow theory, traffic studies, travel demand forecasting, queuing, capacity and level of service, and signalized intersection control. Prerequisite: CIVE 341.

source_quote: Team-oriented, project-based experience in which students work on a meaningful
answer: CIVE 400 Summative Learning (BS) Project, 3(3,0): a team project on an industry or community problem involving literature review, design, data collection, experimentation, analysis, report and presentation. Prerequisites: ENGL 217 and Senior Standing.

source_quote: Principles of structural modeling of different types of structural elements: trusses,
answer: CIVE 413 Computer Modeling of Structures, 3(3,0): modeling trusses, beams, columns, frames and buildings under vertical and lateral loads using structural analysis software. Prerequisite: CIVE 312.

source_quote: Short columns, slender columns, uniaxially and biaxially bent columns; two-way slab
answer: CIVE 415 Concrete II, 3(3,0): short and slender columns, biaxial bending, two-way slabs, retaining walls, wall and column footings, combined footings and staircases.

source_quote: Prerequisite: CIVE 312 and CIVE 314. Annually.
answer: The prerequisites for CIVE 415 Concrete II are CIVE 312 and CIVE 314.

source_quote: Structural steel properties, loads, design methods, analysis, and design of members
answer: CIVE 417 Steel Structures, 3(3,0): steel properties, loads, design methods and design of tension, compression and flexural members and connections. Prerequisite: CIVE 312.

source_quote: Soil classification; origin of soil and grain size; soil structure, weight-volume
answer: CIVE 423 Soil Mechanics, 3(3,0): soil classification, weight-volume relationships, plasticity, compaction, permeability, seepage, stresses, consolidation and shear strength.

source_quote: soil. Prerequisites: MECH 320 and GEOL 221. Annually.
answer: The prerequisites for CIVE 423 Soil Mechanics are MECH 320 and GEOL 221.

source_quote: Experimental testing of soil: Sieve Analysis, Atterberg Limits, Proctor test; sand cone
answer: CIVE 423L Soil Mechanics Laboratory, 1(0,2): sieve analysis, Atterberg limits, Proctor test, sand cone field density, consolidation and direct shear tests with report writing. Co-requisite: CIVE 423.

source_quote: Geotechnical site investigation; field and laboratory tests; characterization of strata;
answer: CIVE 424 Foundation Engineering, 3(3,0): site investigation, bearing capacity and settlement of shallow foundations (footings, mats) and deep foundations (piles), water table effects, mat design and pile load tests. Prerequisite: CIVE 423.

source_quote: Chemical and biological processes related to environmental science and engineering,
answer: CIVE 432 Environmental Engineering, 3(3,0): chemical and biological processes, mass and energy balances, water and wastewater treatment, water quality, air and noise pollution and solid waste management. Prerequisite: CHEM 211.

source_quote: Engineering approaches to the measurement, control, and conveyance of water flows,
answer: CIVE 435 Hydraulics, 3(3,0): measuring, controlling and conveying water flows, hydraulic models, and design of water and wastewater systems. Prerequisite: MECH 333.

source_quote: This Co-op work experience is designed to provide students with an eight-week short-
answer: CIVE 499 Co-op Work Experience, 3(3,0): an eight-week placement in civil and environmental engineering industry, academia or government. Prerequisites: ENGL 217; Senior Standing.

source_quote: Fundamental elements of management of civil engineering projects; roles of all
answer: CIVE 501 Construction Planning and Management, 3(3,0): roles of owners, designers, contractors and suppliers, contracts, estimating, planning and control, CPM, resource scheduling, financing and cost/schedule relationships. Prerequisite: Senior standing.

source_quote: Statically indeterminate structures, force method (beams, trusses, and frames).
answer: CIVE 507 Structural Analysis II, 3(3,0): indeterminate structures by the force method, cable-supported structures, temperature and settlement effects, slope-deflection and moment distribution, and qualitative influence lines. Prerequisite: CIVE 312.

source_quote: its practical applications in civil engineering. The course includes hands-on
answer: CIVE 508 AI Applications in Civil Engineering, 3(3,0): AI fundamentals and practical applications in civil engineering with hands-on programming, real project case studies and AI tools. Prerequisite: CCEE 214.
